kinds.title: Decisions
kinds.description: Every architecture decision this repository has recorded, with what it supersedes, what it put in force, and what has since referred back to it. One page per decision, generated from the decision's own file.

kinds.title: Rules
kinds.description: Every rule in force here — the vendored doctrine package and this repository's own — with the class it declares, the artefacts it names as its enforcement, whether the tree holds them, and the rules either side of it in the dependency graph.

catalogue.reason: A critique is the adversarial pass over one intent's plan, written for the worker who must resolve its findings before work starts (ADR 0073). It is planning state of this repository; what the plan became is published on /plan/.

A deployment object carries the target a release is published to. Its rendered artifacts are in the repository and its state is on the Cockpit; a public page would say only what /docs/install/ already says.
The distribution model is the input the release matrix, the installer and /docs/install/ are all generated from. The generated pages are the publication; the model behind them is not a second one.
A document of the layer is prose already published where it belongs — /docs/, /method/, /context/ — and a second address for the same words is the duplication this file exists to prevent.

A gap is what one worker observed of the repository against an intent's criteria at one commit (ADR 0073). It is a dated input to planning, superseded by the next observation, and the work it suggested is published on /plan/.
An implementation object is a source file a claim names. It is reachable from the claim that names it and from the repository; a page rendering a Rust module is the source browser GitHub already is.

An intent's stage and criteria are derived on every read from the plan and the evidence ledger (ADR 0070); a static page would freeze a derivation at the commit the site was built from. The milestones that realise an intent are published on /plan/, and `majordomus intent show` answers for the intent itself.
Curated knowledge is written for the worker reading the layer, not for a visitor: it is the orientation a session starts from, and it changes with the work rather than with the product.
The mesh declaration is one checkout's identity on the local network. It is operational state of an installation, not a fact about the product.
A prompt is an input to a provider, rendered with the repository's own state. Published on its own it would read as documentation of something a visitor cannot run.
The scope declares which paths of this checkout the tool reads. It is a fact about this repository's layout, and /context/ is where a visitor is told about layout.
A test object is a case file. What it proves is published — on /guarantees/ for the claim and on the rule's own page for the rule — and that is the direction a reader asks in.
A workspace records an external place work is done (a ChatGPT project, an issue tracker). It names accounts and surfaces of the people working here, not of the product.
